3	file: "src/Setoid/Subalgebras/Subdirect/Basic.lagda.md"
4	title: "Setoid.Subalgebras.Subdirect.Basic module (The Agda Universal Algebra Library)"
5	date: "2026-06-20"
6	author: "the agda-algebras development team"
7	---
8	
9	### Subdirect product basics
10	
11	This is the [Setoid.Subalgebras.Subdirect.Basic][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
12	
13	A **subdirect product** of a family `𝒜 : I → Algebra` is a subalgebra of the product
14	`⨅ 𝒜` whose every coordinate projection is *surjective* — the subalgebra meets every
15	factor.  A **subdirect embedding** of `𝑨` is a monomorphism `𝑨 ↪ ⨅ 𝒜` exhibiting `𝑨`
16	as such a subdirect product.  These are the structures underlying Birkhoff's *subdirect
17	representation theorem*: every algebra is a subdirect product of subdirectly irreducible
18	algebras.
19	
20	
21	<!--
22	```agda
23	{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}
24	
25	module Setoid.Subalgebras.Subdirect.Basic where
26	
27	open import Agda.Primitive using () renaming ( Set to Type )
28	
29	-- Imports from the Agda Standard Library -------------------------------------
30	open import Data.Product                           using  ( _,_ ; Σ-syntax
31	                                                          ; proj₁ ; proj₂ )
32	open import Function                               using  ( id )
33	open import Level                                  using  ( Level ; _⊔_ )
34	open import Relation.Binary                        using  ( Setoid )
35	open import Relation.Binary.PropositionalEquality  using  ( _≡_ ; refl )
36	
37	-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library ----------------------------
38	open import Overture                  using  ( 𝓞 ; 𝓥 ; Signature ; 𝑆 )
39	open import Setoid.Algebras           using  ( Algebra ; ⨅ ; 𝔻[_] )
40	open import Setoid.Congruences        using  ( Con ; _╱_ )
41	open import Setoid.Functions          using  ( IsInjective ; IsSurjective )
42	
43	open import Setoid.Homomorphisms      using  ( hom ; IsEpi ; 𝒾𝒹 ; ⊙-hom ; ⨅-hom-co
44	                                             ; πhom ; πepi ; ⨅-proj )
45	open import Setoid.Subalgebras.Basic  using  ( _≤_ )
46	
47	
48	private variable α ρ β ρᵇ ℓ ι : Level
49	```
50	-->
51	
52	#### Subdirect products and subdirect embeddings
53	
54	Fix a candidate algebra `𝑩` and a factor family `𝒜`.  The `i`-th **coordinate map**
55	of a homomorphism `h : 𝑩 → ⨅ 𝒜` is the composite `projᵢ ∘ h : 𝑩 → 𝒜 i`.
56	The homomorphism `h : 𝑩 → ⨅ 𝒜` is a **subdirect embedding** when it is injective and
57	every coordinate map is surjective.
58	
59	```agda
60	module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥}{I : Type ι}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ}(𝒜 : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ) where
61	
62	  -- The i-th coordinate map projᵢ ∘ h of a hom into the product.
63	  coord : hom 𝑩 (⨅ 𝒜) → (i : I) → hom 𝑩 (𝒜 i)
64	  coord h i = ⊙-hom h (⨅-proj 𝒜 i)
65	
66	  record IsSubdirectEmbedding (h : hom 𝑩 (⨅ 𝒜)) : Type (ι ⊔ α ⊔ ρ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ) where
67	    field
68	      embed-inj  : IsInjective (proj₁ h)
69	      proj-onto  : (i : I) → IsSurjective (proj₁ (coord h i))
70	
71	  open IsSubdirectEmbedding public
72	
73	  -- A subdirect embedding of 𝑩 into ⨅ 𝒜;  i.e., 𝑩 is a subdirect product of 𝒜.
74	  SubdirectEmbedding : Type (𝓞 ⊔ 𝓥 ⊔ ι ⊔ α ⊔ ρ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ)
75	  SubdirectEmbedding = Σ[ h ∈ hom 𝑩 (⨅ 𝒜) ] IsSubdirectEmbedding h
76	
77	  -- A subdirect embedding is in particular a subalgebra inclusion 𝑩 ≤ ⨅ 𝒜.
78	  subdirect→≤ : SubdirectEmbedding → 𝑩 ≤ ⨅ 𝒜
79	  subdirect→≤ (h , emb) = h , embed-inj emb
80	```
81	
82	#### The bridge: a separating family of congruences gives a subdirect embedding
83	
84	Now the constructive heart.  Fix an algebra `𝑨` and a family of congruences
85	`θ : I → Con 𝑨`.  Form the family of quotients `i ↦ 𝑨 ╱ θ i` and the natural map
86	into their product, assembled from the canonical quotient projections `πhom (θ i)`.
87	
88	```agda
89	module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥}{I : Type ι}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ}(θ : I → Con 𝑨 ℓ) where
90	  -- the family of quotient algebras and the natural map into their product
91	  𝑨╱ : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ℓ
92	  𝑨╱ i = 𝑨 ╱ θ i
93	
94	  natmap : hom 𝑨 (⨅ 𝑨╱)
95	  natmap = ⨅-hom-co 𝑨╱ (λ i → πhom 𝒾𝒹 (θ i))
96	```
97	
98	The family **separates points** when the only pairs related by *every* `θ i` are the
99	`≈`-equal ones — i.e. the meet `⋂ θ` is the diagonal `0ᴬ`.  This is *exactly* the
100	injectivity of the natural map: an element's image in the product is its tuple of
101	congruence classes, and two elements have the same tuple iff every `θ i` relates
102	them.
103	
104	```agda
105	
106	  -- the meet ⋂ θ is the diagonal 0ᴬ: every θ i relating a,b forces a ≈ b.
107	  Separates : Type (ι ⊔ α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
108	  Separates = ∀ {a b} → (∀ i → proj₁ (θ i) a b) → a ≈ b
109	    where open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] using ( _≈_ )
110	  -- Injectivity of the natural map is definitionally the separation property.
111	  natmap-injective : Separates → IsInjective (proj₁ natmap)
112	  natmap-injective = id
113	
114	  natmap-separates : IsInjective (proj₁ natmap) → Separates
115	  natmap-separates = id
116	
117	  _ : IsInjective (proj₁ natmap) ≡ Separates
118	  _ = refl
119	```
120	
121	Each coordinate map `projᵢ ∘ natmap` *is* the canonical quotient epimorphism
122	`𝑨 ↠ 𝑨 ╱ θ i`, hence surjective — with no decidability or choice assumption on the
123	index.
124	
125	```agda
126	  natmap-proj-onto : (i : I) → IsSurjective (proj₁ (coord 𝑨╱ natmap i))
127	  natmap-proj-onto i = IsEpi.isSurjective (proj₂ (πepi 𝒾𝒹 (θ i)))
128	```
129	
130	Assembling injectivity and the surjective coordinate maps gives the subdirect embedding.
131	
132	```agda
133	  separating→subdirect : Separates → IsSubdirectEmbedding 𝑨╱ natmap
134	  separating→subdirect sep = record  { embed-inj = natmap-injective sep
135	                                     ; proj-onto = natmap-proj-onto }
136	
137	  separating→SubdirectEmbedding : Separates → SubdirectEmbedding 𝑨╱
138	  separating→SubdirectEmbedding sep = natmap , separating→subdirect sep
139	```

```agda
private variable α ρ β ρᵇ ℓ ι : Level
```

#### Subdirect products and subdirect embeddings

Fix a candidate algebra `𝑩` and a factor family `𝒜`.  The `i`-th **coordinate map**
of a homomorphism `h : 𝑩 → ⨅ 𝒜` is the composite `projᵢ ∘ h : 𝑩 → 𝒜 i`.

every coordinate map is surjective.

```agda
module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥}{I : Type ι}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ}(𝒜 : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ) where

  -- The i-th coordinate map projᵢ ∘ h of a hom into the product.
  coord : hom 𝑩 (⨅ 𝒜) → (i : I) → hom 𝑩 (𝒜 i)
  coord h i = ⊙-hom h (⨅-proj 𝒜 i)

  record IsSubdirectEmbedding (h : hom 𝑩 (⨅ 𝒜)) : Type (ι ⊔ α ⊔ ρ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ) where
    field
      embed-inj  : IsInjective (proj₁ h)
      proj-onto  : (i : I) → IsSurjective (proj₁ (coord h i))

  open IsSubdirectEmbedding public

  -- A subdirect embedding of 𝑩 into ⨅ 𝒜;  i.e., 𝑩 is a subdirect product of 𝒜.
  SubdirectEmbedding : Type (𝓞 ⊔ 𝓥 ⊔ ι ⊔ α ⊔ ρ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ)
  SubdirectEmbedding = Σ[ h ∈ hom 𝑩 (⨅ 𝒜) ] IsSubdirectEmbedding h

  -- A subdirect embedding is in particular a subalgebra inclusion 𝑩 ≤ ⨅ 𝒜.
  subdirect→≤ : SubdirectEmbedding → 𝑩 ≤ ⨅ 𝒜
  subdirect→≤ (h , emb) = h , embed-inj emb
```

#### The bridge: a separating family of congruences gives a subdirect embedding

Now the constructive heart.  Fix an algebra `𝑨` and a family of congruences
`θ : I → Con 𝑨`.  Form the family of quotients `i ↦ 𝑨 ╱ θ i` and the natural map
into their product, assembled from the canonical quotient projections `πhom (θ i)`.

```agda
module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥}{I : Type ι}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ}(θ : I → Con 𝑨 ℓ) where
  -- the family of quotient algebras and the natural map into their product
  𝑨╱ : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ℓ
  𝑨╱ i = 𝑨 ╱ θ i

  natmap : hom 𝑨 (⨅ 𝑨╱)
  natmap = ⨅-hom-co 𝑨╱ (λ i → πhom 𝒾𝒹 (θ i))
```

The family **separates points** when the only pairs related by *every* `θ i` are the
`≈`-equal ones — i.e. the meet `⋂ θ` is the diagonal `0ᴬ`.  This is *exactly* the
injectivity of the natural map: an element's image in the product is its tuple of
congruence classes, and two elements have the same tuple iff every `θ i` relates
them.

```agda

  -- the meet ⋂ θ is the diagonal 0ᴬ: every θ i relating a,b forces a ≈ b.
  Separates : Type (ι ⊔ α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
  Separates = ∀ {a b} → (∀ i → proj₁ (θ i) a b) → a ≈ b
    where open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] using ( _≈_ )
  -- Injectivity of the natural map is definitionally the separation property.
  natmap-injective : Separates → IsInjective (proj₁ natmap)
  natmap-injective = id

  natmap-separates : IsInjective (proj₁ natmap) → Separates
  natmap-separates = id

  _ : IsInjective (proj₁ natmap) ≡ Separates
  _ = refl
```

Each coordinate map `projᵢ ∘ natmap` *is* the canonical quotient epimorphism
`𝑨 ↠ 𝑨 ╱ θ i`, hence surjective — with no decidability or choice assumption on the
index.

```agda
  natmap-proj-onto : (i : I) → IsSurjective (proj₁ (coord 𝑨╱ natmap i))
  natmap-proj-onto i = IsEpi.isSurjective (proj₂ (πepi 𝒾𝒹 (θ i)))
```

Assembling injectivity and the surjective coordinate maps gives the subdirect embedding.

```agda
  separating→subdirect : Separates → IsSubdirectEmbedding 𝑨╱ natmap
  separating→subdirect sep = record  { embed-inj = natmap-injective sep
                                     ; proj-onto = natmap-proj-onto }

  separating→SubdirectEmbedding : Separates → SubdirectEmbedding 𝑨╱
  separating→SubdirectEmbedding sep = natmap , separating→subdirect sep
```

carrier of `𝑩`.[^1]

so it is a *preorder*; that is exactly what [Setoid.Subalgebras.Properties][]
proves, as `≤-preorder`{.AgdaFunction}, and it is the only order-theoretic fact
about `_≤_`{.AgdaFunction} that this subtree establishes.

It is not a partial order.  Antisymmetry would require that `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩` and `𝑩 ≤ 𝑨`

too: `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩` and `𝑩 ≤ 𝑨` supply injective homomorphisms in both directions, and a

in general no isomorphism need exist at all — the free groups on two and on three

yields classically need not be a homomorphism.

surjective; and an injective, surjective homomorphism is an isomorphism, by

smaller algebra with the larger one fixed, and relative to a whole class rather
